info.title: Paddock Runner API
info.description:
The complete HTTP surface of one Paddock runner (one served model, one port).

The surface has three families:

- **OpenAI-compatible** - `/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/completions`, `/v1/responses`, `/v1/embeddings`, `/v1/audio/transcriptions`, `/v1/models`. These conform to OpenAI's API and are documented by OpenAI's own reference; this document lists them with Paddock's deviations and extensions only, and deliberately does not re-specify their schemas. Point an official OpenAI SDK at the runner's base URL and it works.
- **Anthropic-compatible** - `/v1/messages`, `/v1/messages/count_tokens`. Same rule: Anthropic's reference is the specification.
- **Paddock-native** - forced alignment, rerank, dense prediction (`/v1/segmentations`), the extraction preview, the model card, stats, and the realtime socket. These exist nowhere else, so they are fully specified here.

Authentication: a runner started without an API key accepts unauthenticated requests. With a key configured, `/v1/*` and `/api/*` require `Authorization: Bearer <key>`; `/healthz` and this document stay open, and `/metrics` is open on loopback but keyed over the network.

One runner serves one model, so `model` request fields are accepted and ignored everywhere; `GET /v1/models` lists exactly one entry with Paddock capability extensions.

servers.description: A runner endpoint. The manager allocates ports upward from 11540; hand-started runners use whatever their config names.

tags.name: openai
tags.description: OpenAI-compatible - specified by OpenAI's reference; deviations and extensions noted per operation

post.description: Three explicit contracts: prepared runs the neural core on caller-transformed numerical matrices; sdm_v1 fits the SDM numerical/categorical recipe on context only and ensembles predictions; context_id reuses a fitted GPU context. sdm_v1 includes constant-column removal, F64 standardization, four round-robin transforms, outlier clipping, categorical alignment/counts, seeded signs/Latin feature permutations/label shifts and target inversion. Its portable seed is not PyTorch RNG-compatible. Classification supports at most ten classes (no ECOC). Missing features are null; unknown raw categories map to -1. Raw numbers are bounded to ±1e30 and category strings to 4096 bytes. The optional model must match the served id. Total prepared context + query cells must not exceed 131072; body limit 8 MiB. No chat or JEV semantics.

200.description: object=tabular.prediction; model, task, preprocessing, predictions and usage. Classification predictions contain class, probabilities and logits in code order. Regression predictions contain median and 999 sorted quantiles, with shared quantile_levels 0.001..0.999. Usage reports context_rows, query_rows, columns, GPU milliseconds, elapsed milliseconds and workspace bytes (not tokens).

400.description: Invalid table, class codes or preprocessing contract

401.description: Missing or invalid configured runner key

404.description: Requested model id is not served, or context was expired, evicted or released

503.description: No tabular model loaded, queue full, draining or admission cap reached

500.description: Inference or memory-budget failure; no prediction returned

post.summary: Fit preprocessing and GPU attention context
post.description: Accepts sdm_v1 context, targets and column types; query must be absent or empty. Returns context_id, classes, num_estimators, recipe_seed, cache_bytes and measured usage. Opaque IDs are scoped to this runner and its authentication boundary. All original context processing is performed once per estimator. At most four contexts; idle TTL 600 seconds, LRU eviction, cache budget at most 1 GiB and one quarter of available model budget after weights (including retained host recipe allocations). Expired/evicted IDs return 404, never silent recomputation. Contexts are memory-only and do not survive runner restart. Failed or abandoned fits release their allocations.

400.description: Invalid table or ensemble exceeds cache budget

503.description: Queue full, draining or admission cap reached

delete.description: Serialized with inference on the owning thread; buffers are never freed while the GPU uses them. Requires the same runner authentication as predictions.

404.description: Unknown, expired, evicted or previously released context

200.description: Serving. Body is the literal text `ok`.

503.description: Draining: finishing in-flight requests, refusing new ones. Body is the literal text `draining`.

get.description: Prometheus text exposition (request counters, token counters, latency histograms, engine gauges). Open on loopback; over the network it requires the bearer key when one is configured.

get.summary: List the served model (OpenAI shape + Paddock capability extensions)
get.description: OpenAI's list shape with one entry per serving role on this runner. Each entry additionally carries honest capability metadata: input/output modalities, `capabilities` (e.g. `vision`, `audio`, `alignment` with `alignment_max_clip_s`, `timestamp_granularities`, `include`), and the context window - so a client learns what a request can ask for without discovering it from a 400.

post.description: Conforms to OpenAI Chat Completions: streaming semantics, tool calling incl. parallel tool calls, structured outputs, vision content parts, logprobs, and OpenAI error shapes. `model` is accepted and ignored (one model per runner). See the conformance matrix for the honored-parameter list.

200.description: Completion object, or an SSE stream when `stream: true`

post.description: The legacy text-completions surface, kept because benchmark tools and older clients still speak it. Supports `logprobs` in the legacy shape.

200.description: Completion object, or an SSE stream when `stream: true`

post.description: The items + event-stream model agent SDKs are converging on - first-class in Paddock alongside Chat Completions: typed event stream, tool calling, reasoning items, MCP server tools, `max_tool_calls`. `previous_response_id` continuation is supported for MCP approval flows only.

200.description: Response object, or the typed SSE event stream when `stream: true`

post.description: The compaction executor standalone, returning OpenAI's `CompactedResponse` shape (object `response.compaction`): the conversation's user items followed by one compaction item, with the summarization pass's usage.
Conforms to Anthropic's Messages API: streaming event shapes, tool use, thinking blocks, vision content, and Anthropic error shapes. `model` is accepted and ignored.

200.description: Message object, or the Anthropic SSE stream when `stream: true`

post.description: Real tokenizer, real attachment extraction - the number a send would actually cost, never an estimate.
Served by encoder models (embeddings/reranker checkpoints). Supports `dimensions` (Matryoshka truncation) and `encoding_format`.

Paddock-native (the shape follows the industry rerank convention). Served by reranker models - encoder checkpoints whose vocabulary carries the yes/no relevance tokens; `GET /v1/models` advertises `rerank` capability. Results come back sorted by descending relevance.

post.summary: Structured read: fixed questions about a text, answered with probabilities
post.description: Paddock-native, in the Jev `/v1/systemone` shape. Served only by a block-diffusion model (DiffusionGemma): `GET /api/server` carries `structured_read` with the canvas width and the per-call caps, and every other model answers 400. `state` is the text; `questions` maps an id (one word, no `:`) to a typed question - `noul` (also `bool`/`boolean`: a yes/no probability, optional `criteria: {true, false}` descriptions), `choice` (`criteria` maps option names to descriptions), `score` (`criteria` is the ordered list of level names). Every question is read in ONE denoising pass over the seeded answer template, so each answer is a full distribution over its labels rather than a sampled token, and the mass the model put OUTSIDE the label set comes back as `outside`. `samples` is `"auto"` (one read, then re-reads with fresh slot noise while any slot's entropy is above `auto_threshold`, up to `auto_max` in all) or an integer 1..max_samples. Labels must be single tokens that change exactly one template position; a label set that does not is refused by name (422), as is a state whose prompt plus canvas exceeds the window. Refused: `images`, `steps` other than 1, conditional questions (`depends_on`, `ask_if`, `alone`).

200.description: One typed answer per question, plus the read's diagnostics

422.description: The question set or the state was refused; the message names the question, or the window

post.description:
Conforms to OpenAI's transcription surface: multipart `file`, `language`, `languages[]`, `prompt`, `response_format` (`json`, `text`, `srt`, `vtt`, `verbose_json`), `timestamp_granularities[]`, streaming `transcript.text.*` SSE. Paddock extensions, all advertised per model in `/v1/models` and `/api/server` so clients never discover them from a 400: `include[]=logprobs` yields per-word confidence (`paddock_confidence`, `paddock_alt`, `paddock_margin`) on lanes with no timestamp vocabulary; decode-guard annotations report spans the model refused or cut rather than silently dropping them.

**Language.** `language` FORCES one and skips detection; `languages[]` is OpenAI's plural and is honoured here as a SOFT PRIOR over the server's own detection - it biases, it never filters, so a language nobody named still wins when the audio says so. The two are mutually exclusive and a code outside the loaded checkpoint's map is a 400 rather than a failed decode; the map itself is published as `language_detection.languages`. Every JSON body carries `paddock_language`: where the reported code came from (`asked` / `detected` / `reported` / `unknown`), its probability and runners-up where a detector produced them, whether a hint overturned the model's own answer, and what language the finished TEXT reads as. When that last one contradicts the language the decode ran under, a `language_mismatch` decode-guard notice says so on every body shape - a speech model told the wrong language translates rather than transcribes, and that failure is otherwise fluent, grammatical and invisible.

200.description: Transcription in the requested `response_format`, or the SSE stream

get.description:
Paddock-native protocol, not OpenAI Realtime transcription. Upgrade with the same runner Bearer authentication. Send binary mono 16-kHz signed PCM16 little-endian messages, 1–16000 samples each, then a JSON text message {"type":"finish"}. No base64, compressed containers, midstream reconfiguration or resume. Unknown controls and odd/empty binary messages fail. One session is one recording, limited to 600 seconds of audio, 60 seconds without audio, 900 seconds total wall time. Socket output has a ten-second send deadline. All file/live sessions share two admission slots and one owning inference worker; idle sessions do not hold the worker. Disconnect discards its speaker state. In-flight sessions are counted during runner drain.

The server sends diarization.session (sequence_number=0), one diarization.update per accepted binary message, then exactly one diarization.done after finish. Sequence numbers increase by one, including lookahead-only updates. Updates carry received_samples, frames, finalized_through_seconds, gpu_seconds, completed and active. completed contains newly closed, append-only segments; active is a REPLACEMENT snapshot of at most eight open segments. An open segment keeps its (speaker,start) key until it appears in completed. Do not append active snapshots to history. At done, active is empty and completed flushes the final intervals. Interval seconds use the original untrimmed PCM timeline; overlap is preserved. Sort accumulated completed by (start,speaker) to recover file-result order. No complete recording/timeline is retained by the server.

Input buffering: offline 30.4s, low 1.04s, very_low 0.64s, ultra_low 0.32s, plus 0.006s centered-FFT lookahead and execution time. An error emits diarization.error with sequence_number and error.{type,message}, then closes. No completion is implied after error or disconnect. Message/frame size violations close at the WebSocket protocol layer. File POST remains non-streaming; discovery advertises this separate path under realtime_diarization.

parameters.name: model
parameters.description: If supplied, must match the served id

101.description: WebSocket upgraded; JSON text events and binary PCM input

400.description: Invalid query, model role or upgrade

429.description: No session capacity; Retry-After header supplied

503.description: Worker unavailable or runner draining; Retry-After supplied

post.summary: Speaker diarization: who spoke when, including overlap
post.description: Paddock-native, not an OpenAI transcription endpoint. Nemotron 3 Diarization serves eight anonymous arrival-order speaker channels at 10-ms resolution. No transcript, named-person recognition or ASR sidecar is implied. A file is processed through bounded speaker-cache/FIFO windows; its timestamps are relative to the original untrimmed audio. This HTTP operation returns one final result, not a live network stream. Limits: 25 MiB multipart body, 0.01–600 seconds of decoded audio, two admitted uploads/jobs. Corrupt or changing audio streams are rejected rather than silently shifting timestamps.

file.description: WAV, FLAC, MP3, MP4/M4A, OGG or WebM; downmixed and resampled to mono 16 kHz

model.description: If supplied, must match the served model ID

words.description: Optional JSON array (at most 20000 entries / 2 MiB) of existing ASR word records: word, optional start/end in seconds, other metadata preserved. Finite complete intervals must lie inside this recording. No text recognition or timestamp synthesis. Returned attribution uses duration overlap: speakers contains every channel covering at least half the word; speaker is null unless exactly one qualifies. Silence, untimed and zero-duration words abstain; several candidates are ambiguous, not identified people. speaker_coverage is eight duration fractions, not confidence.
Original word records enriched with speaker, speakers, speaker_status and speaker_coverage; null when not requested

gpu_seconds.description: Measured command time, including the GPU audio frontend

404.description: The requested model is not served

429.description: Shared file/live session admission is full; Retry-After supplied

503.description: Worker unavailable or runner draining; Retry-After supplied

post.summary: Forced alignment: word times for an existing transcript
post.description:
Paddock-native - no OpenAI equivalent exists. Audio + the transcript to align go in; per-word start/end times come out, in exactly `verbose_json`'s word shape so any client that parses OpenAI word timestamps parses this unchanged. Served by forced-aligner models (`alignment` capability in `/v1/models`).

Limits, both refused loudly with the number in the message: one call addresses at most the model's time-bin budget (400 s on the 0.6B aligner - align longer audio per segment and offset the times), and the packed sequence must fit the model context. Japanese/Korean are refused (they need morphological word tokenizers this server does not carry). Languages outside the model's trained set are accepted and flagged `language_supported: false`.

The aligner times whatever text it is given - a wrong transcript gets confidently wrong times. It is a timing tool, not a correction tool.

file.description: The audio clip (same container support as /v1/audio/transcriptions)

text.description: The transcript to align. `transcript` is accepted as an alias.

language.description: Language as ISO 639-1 code or English name (both value spaces accepted). Optional; feeds the `language_supported` flag.

model.description: Accepted and ignored - one model per runner.

503.description: No forced-alignment model is loaded on this runner

post.description:
Served by image-generation models (`image_generation` capability in `/v1/models`; today Qwen-Image-2.1). The GPT-image-model form of the OpenAI Images API: images always come back as `b64_json`, `size` is any `WIDTHxHEIGHT` on the model's grid (`image_generation.size_multiple` in `GET /api/server`, 32 here) up to `max_side`, `output_format` selects png (default, keeps alpha) / webp / jpeg, `background: transparent` asks the model for an RGBA image, `quality` picks the step count (`low` 20, `medium` 30, otherwise the model's own 40). DALL-E fields (`style`, `response_format: url`) are refused by name; streaming and partial images are not served yet.

Paddock extras on the same object: `seed` (default 42), `steps` (1..100), `guidance` (classifier-free guidance scale, off at <= 1, the model's default), `negative_prompt` (with guidance > 1), and `width` / `height` instead of `size`. Same seed, same request, same server: the same bytes.

400.description: Invalid request (an off-grid size, a DALL-E-only field, an unsupported option)

503.description: No image-generation model is loaded on this runner

post.summary: Image editing (OpenAI Images API) - not served yet
post.description: The route exists so a client learns the truth in one round trip: this build serves text-to-image only. Editing with reference images (the model supports up to 10) is the next phase of the image lane; until then every request here is refused with 400.

400.description: Image editing is not served by this build

503.description: No image-generation model is loaded on this runner

post.summary: Dense prediction: image chips in, class and regression rasters out
post.description:
Paddock-native - no OpenAI equivalent exists. Served by dense-prediction models (`segmentation` capability in `/v1/models`; today `tic-forestry-v1`, which reads 512x512 four-band aerial chips at 0.5 m and returns a land-cover class raster and a canopy-height raster at 1 m). Built for sweeps over an area: one request carries many chips, and the server packs chips from all in-flight requests into fixed-width passes. Every pass runs at the endpoint's one width (short ones are padded), so a chip's rasters depend on the chip and the endpoint's configuration and never on what else was queued - the price is that a lone chip costs a whole pass.

Two request forms, told apart by Content-Type. `multipart/form-data`: one or more `image` parts, each a TIFF (detected by its magic bytes) or a raw block. Any other Content-Type: the body is N raw blocks back to back, with the options below in the query string. A raw block is exactly `input.chip_bytes` from `GET /api/server` - u8, row-major, bands interleaved in `input.bands` order.

Nothing is resampled or reprojected. A TIFF of the wrong size, band count or ground sample distance is refused with the mismatch named, because the model would serve it without complaint and be wrong.

The regression raster is unclamped: a negative canopy height is the model being wrong near an edge, not a sentinel.

parameters.name: response_format
parameters.description: Raw-body form only; the multipart form carries this as a field.

parameters.name: logits
parameters.description: Raw-body form only; the multipart form carries this as a field.

image.description: One part per chip (`image[]` and `file` are accepted spellings). A GeoTIFF's tiepoint, pixel scale and EPSG code are carried onto the output as `georeference`.

logits.description: Also return the class logits (f16, pixel-major) - about twenty times the class raster.

200.description: `json`: an embeddings-shaped list; every raster is base64 of little-endian bytes, row-major from the top-left. `binary`: per chip, the class raster (u8), then the regression raster (f32 LE), then the logits if asked for (f16 LE); `x-paddock-chips`, `x-paddock-raster-size`, `x-paddock-classes` and `x-paddock-layout` describe the geometry.

class_names.description: Class code to name, in code order.

regression_name.description: What the regression raster measures, e.g. `canopy_height_m`.

classes.description: base64, u8 per pixel: the argmax class code.

logits.description: base64, f16 LE per pixel per class. Only when asked for.

georeference.description: Where the OUTPUT raster sits on the ground. Only for chips that arrived as GeoTIFFs.

origin_x.description: Map X of the top-left corner.

origin_y.description: Map Y of the top-left corner.

400.description: A chip of the wrong size, band count or ground sample distance; a raw body that is not a whole number of chips; an unknown option. The message names what was found and what the model takes.

503.description: No dense-prediction model is loaded on this runner.

get.description: Paddock-native WebSocket for live speech-to-text: the client streams 16 kHz mono PCM frames; the server runs voice-activity detection and answers utterance-by-utterance transcript events (partials while an utterance is open, a settled item when it closes, with per-word times and confidence where the lane supports them). Requires a served speech-capable model. A plain GET without the upgrade handshake is refused.

get.summary: The model card: what THIS endpoint can answer
get.description: One call, the whole truth about the running configuration: served model ids per role (`model`, `embedder`, `asr`, `aligner`), context window, batch size, reasoning style, sampling defaults, vision/audio/document capabilities with their budgets, `timestamp_granularities`, `include` values, `alignment_max_clip_s`, task tags, PDF handling, server-side tools (web search, MCP server labels), aliases and variants. Keys are additive across versions; absent means the capability is absent.

post.summary: Extraction preview: what the model would read from an attachment
post.description: Runs the same extraction lanes a chat send runs (PDF text, docx, spreadsheets, text-native decode, photo metadata) and returns the injection text verbatim - metadata block included - so a client can show exactly what a prompt will carry. Refusals (encrypted PDF, undecodable bytes) are the same honest 400s a send would produce.

data.description: The file as a data URI or bare base64

filename.description: Original filename, used for type detection

file_metadata.description: Whether the metadata block rides along (default on) - same contract as the inference surfaces

pages.description: Page count where the lane has one

post.summary: Embedded file metadata: everything the file says about itself
post.description: Every metadata field a file carries, grouped by source - EXIF, MakerNotes, XMP, IPTC, ICC, PDF Info, QuickTime and derived Composite tags for photos and documents; core.xml, app.xml and custom.xml properties for Office packages. Distinct from /api/extract, which answers what the MODEL would read and is shaped by this server's context window and vision capability: this one depends on nothing but the bytes. A file that carries no metadata is an ordinary empty answer, not an error.

data.description: The file as a data URI or bare base64

format.description: What the BYTES are ("JPEG", "PDF", "Office Open XML" ...), never the declared mime; null when the magic bytes match nothing we read

groups.description: Groups in reader order; empty when the file carries no metadata

name.description: An open set, named by the reader and the file: EXIF, MakerNotes, XMP, IPTC, ICC, PDF, QuickTime, HEIF, Composite, File - or Document, Application, Custom for Office packages. A group is a namespace: the same name in two groups is two sources stating it, not a duplicate.

value.description: Display-ready; control characters collapse to spaces

truncated.description: Present and true when the value hit the 4096-character ceiling

get.summary: Engine self-report: counters and VRAM ledger
get.description: The runner's inside view: engine counters plus allocator-ledger VRAM. Cheap - returns the last background sample and never blocks inference. The shape is additive across versions.

get.summary: Stats as a live SSE stream
get.description: The same snapshots as `/api/stats`, pushed as server-sent events.

post.summary: Resolve a pending MCP tool-call approval
post.description: A streaming agent loop that hit an approval-required MCP tool is parked on this id. POST the decision to resume it. 404 when the id is unknown - already decided, timed out, or the stream ended.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The approval id from the stream's approval-request event

200.description: Decision accepted; the parked loop resumes

bearerAuth.description: Required on /v1/* and /api/* only when the runner was configured with an API key; a keyless local runner accepts unauthenticated requests.

BadRequest.description: Invalid request - OpenAI-shaped error body with the refusal spelled out

Error.description: The OpenAI-shaped error envelope every surface uses, 404s included

duration.description: Clip length in seconds, as the server measured it

language.description: Echo of the request's language field

language_supported.description: false = outside the model's trained languages; the times still came back and may be useful, but the reader deserves the flag

words.description: One entry per word of the submitted text (punctuation-only tokens dropped, CJK one character at a time), in reading order - verbose_json's word shape

start.description: Seconds from the start of the clip

end.description: Seconds from the start of the clip

model.description: Accepted and ignored - one model per runner

top_n.description: Return only the best N (default: all)

return_documents.description: Echo each document's text back in its result

instruction.description: Task instruction for the relevance judge (a sensible default is used when absent)

index.description: Position in the request's documents array

state.description: The text the questions are about

questions.description: id -> question. Ids are single words without ':' (they are written into the answer template); at most `max_questions` per call (advertised in `structured_read`).

instructions.description: What to decide about the state

criteria.description: noul: optional {true, false} descriptions; choice: option name -> description (2 to 26 options); score: the ordered list of level names (2 to 26)

samples.description: "auto" (the default) or a fixed number of reads per question, 1..max_samples

auto_threshold.description: auto re-reads while any slot's entropy is above this

auto_max.description: auto reads at most this many times in all

seed.description: Slot-noise seed; read k noises with seed + 7919 k

steps.description: Only a single denoising read is served

answers.description: id -> answer, one per question. Every answer carries `confidence` (Jev's measure: (n * max - 1) / (n - 1) over the mean label probabilities, 0 at uniform and 1 at certainty - (3 * max - 1) / 2 for three options; on a noul answer n = 2), `agreement` (the share of reads that picked it) and `outside` (the mass the model put outside the label set at that slot - the calibration signal a top-k logprobs read cannot see).

choice.description: choice: the option with the most mass

score.description: score: the probability-weighted level index, 0 to levels - 1

level.description: score: the level with the most mass

probabilities.description: choice: option -> mean probability; score: level index -> mean probability

canvas.description: Canvas positions used by the answer template

position.description: The slot's position in the canvas

entropy.description: Mean slot entropy over the full vocabulary, in nats

label_mass.description: Mean raw mass on the label set (1 - outside)

reads.description: One entry per read: what this slot picked and how surely - which reads disagreed, not only that some did

ServerCard.description: Keys are additive across versions; the ones below are stable. Absent means the capability is absent.

aligner.description: Served forced-alignment model id - POST /v1/audio/alignments works iff set

diarization.description: Served speaker model and capabilities; POST /v1/audio/diarizations works iff set. This does not enable transcription.

alignment_max_clip_s.description: Longest clip one alignment call can address

structured_read.description: POST /v1/systemone works iff set (a block-diffusion model): {canvas_width, max_questions, max_samples, types}

sampling.description: The server's sampling defaults - what an untouched dial means
